findings.title: Client-side upload limits no longer honor the configured per-type limits
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` now rejects every upload above 10 MB, regardless of whether it is an image or attachment and regardless of `max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb`. Sites configured to allow attachments larger than 10 MB will have those uploads rejected in the browser before the server sees them, and the displayed limit is incorrect. If a fixed pre-downsize ceiling is needed for images, it should be applied only to images while attachments continue to use their configured limit.

findings.title: API URL uploads are capped at 10 MB instead of the configured upload limit
findings.body: Remote uploads supplied through the API are now downloaded with a hard 10 MB limit. This applies before the code knows whether the URL is an image that can be downsized, and therefore also blocks remote attachment uploads that the site's `max_attachment_size_kb` permits. It also prevents configured image limits above 10 MB from being used. Preserve the configured limit for non-images (and use an explicitly documented pre-downsize image ceiling if one is required).

findings.title: The new downsize overload replaces the existing five-argument method in Ruby
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by arity: defining `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Any existing caller using the prior public method signature will now raise `ArgumentError` rather than resize its image. Support both forms in one method (for example with optional arguments or splatting) or update every caller and preserve compatibility for plugin callers.
